_readme: Synthetic historical incidents used to give ATTACKDNA a memory to search. Every organisation, person, address and identifier here is invented. The reports are written UN-sanitized on purpose: seeding runs them through the real Privacy Layer, so the seeded corpus is proof the pipeline works rather than a hand-cleaned shortcut.

incidents.title: Ransomware via phishing link — regional bank
incidents.text: On 14 November 2024 the SOC at Al-Waha Regional Bank detected ransomware activity on WKSTN-FIN-118 in the finance department. Initial access came from a spearphishing link sent to noura.alsaleh@alwaha-bank.com.sa from billing@invoice-portal-secure.com. The user clicked the link and entered credentials on a fake login page. The attacker used the stolen credentials to sign in from 185.220.101.44, then ran encoded PowerShell to disable the EDR agent. They moved laterally over SMB shares to FS-CORP-03, deleted shadow copies, and files were encrypted across two file servers. Customer data was exfiltrated to cloud storage before encryption. Operations were disrupted for 19 hours. Contact CISO Faisal Alharbi at +966 55 214 7788.

mitigations.action: Isolate affected endpoints from the network immediately
mitigations.notes: Containment within 40 minutes stopped spread to the third file server.

mitigations.action: Disable the compromised account and revoke all active sessions and tokens
Block the phishing URL at the proxy and reset credentials for users who clicked
Restore from the most recent verified-clean offline backup
mitigations.notes: Restore took 11 hours against a stated 4-hour RTO.

mitigations.action: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for all users
Enable tamper protection on all endpoint security agents
mitigations.notes: The attacker disabled EDR because tamper protection was off.

incidents.title: Ransomware via unpatched VPN appliance — manufacturing
incidents.text: Al-Mustaqbal Manufacturing Company reported ransomware on 3 February 2025. The attacker exploited a vulnerability in an internet-facing VPN appliance, CVE-2024-21762, to gain access without credentials. From the appliance they pivoted to the production network, performed a network scan of the plant subnet, dumped credentials from LSASS on SRV-APP-07, and moved laterally using RDP. Backups were deleted with vssadmin and files were encrypted across the production line servers. The factory was offline for three days. Incident handled by Eng. Tariq Bin Salem, reachable at tariq.binsalem@mustaqbal-mfg.com. Attacker infrastructure observed at 45.83.192.17.

mitigations.action: Isolate affected endpoints from the network immediately
Patch the exploited service and inspect for web shells left behind
mitigations.notes: The appliance had been unpatched for 7 months.

mitigations.action: Force a domain-wide credential reset, including krbtgt twice
Rebuild affected hosts from image; shadow copies cannot be trusted
Maintain immutable, air-gapped backups and rehearse restore times
mitigations.notes: Immutable backups were adopted after this incident and proved decisive later.

mitigations.action: Segment the OT network from corporate IT with an enforced boundary

incidents.title: Ransomware via compromised MSP — healthcare group
incidents.text: Dar Al-Shifa Hospital Group experienced a ransomware incident on 22 May 2025 originating from its managed service provider. The attacker compromised the MSP's remote management tooling in a supply chain intrusion and pushed a malicious update to 240 endpoints. Obfuscated payloads executed via a signed binary proxy. Security tooling was disabled on affected hosts before the files were encrypted. Patient scheduling systems were unavailable for 26 hours and the regulator was notified. Reported by Dr. Hanan Alqahtani, h.alqahtani@daralshifa.sa. C2 beaconing was observed to 91.219.236.10.

mitigations.action: Isolate affected endpoints from the network immediately
Suspend all third-party remote management access pending vendor assurance
mitigations.notes: The single most effective action; should have been possible in minutes but took four hours.

mitigations.action: Sinkhole the C2 domain and block the destination at the egress firewall
Restore from the most recent verified-clean offline backup
Require vendors to use dedicated, monitored, time-bound access accounts
Enable tamper protection on all endpoint security agents

incidents.title: Business email compromise — logistics
incidents.text: Bahri Freight Logistics LLC suffered a business email compromise discovered on 9 January 2025. A finance officer received a spearphishing link and authenticated on a credential harvesting page. The attacker signed in with the valid account from 103.216.44.90, created an inbox rule to hide replies, and monitored the mailbox for two weeks. They then sent a fraudulent transfer request with amended beneficiary details, resulting in a wire transfer of SAR 1,400,000. Financial loss was partially recovered. Reported by Manager Salma Alotaibi, salma.o@bahrifreight.com.

mitigations.action: Freeze the transaction and notify the receiving bank within the recall window
mitigations.notes: Only 40% of funds recovered; the recall window had nearly closed.

mitigations.action: Disable the compromised account and revoke all active sessions and tokens
Audit all mailboxes for attacker-created inbox rules
mitigations.notes: Two additional compromised mailboxes were found this way.

mitigations.action: Require out-of-band verification for payment-detail changes
mitigations.notes: This control alone would have prevented the loss.

mitigations.action: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for all users
Alert on OAuth consent grants and logins from unfamiliar ASNs

incidents.title: Credential harvesting phishing campaign — university
incidents.text: King Abdulwahab University reported a phishing campaign on 18 March 2025. A malicious link was distributed to 3,100 student and staff addresses from a newly registered domain, university-portal-login.top. 62 users entered credentials on the fake login page. Valid accounts were then used to send further phishing internally. No malware executed and no data was exfiltrated. The campaign was reported by Analyst Yousef Almutairi at y.almutairi@kau-example.edu.sa. Source addresses included 194.5.53.201.

mitigations.action: Quarantine the delivered message across all mailboxes and block the sender
Block the phishing URL at the proxy and reset credentials for users who clicked
Disable the compromised account and revoke all active sessions and tokens
Enable URL rewriting/detonation and attachment sandboxing on the mail gateway
Alert on first-time-seen sender domains targeting finance and executive users

incidents.title: Web application exploitation and data breach — e-commerce
incidents.text: Souq Alkhaleej Trading Ltd disclosed a data breach on 27 April 2025. An attacker exploited a SQL injection flaw in a public-facing application and deployed a web shell on the web server. They enumerated the customer database and exfiltrated approximately 180,000 customer records over an encrypted channel to an external host at 176.113.115.34. The intrusion was undetected for 11 days. Regulatory notification obligations were triggered. Contact was Director Maha Alfarsi, maha@souqalkhaleej.com.

mitigations.action: Take the affected application offline and preserve forensic images
Patch the exploited service and inspect for web shells left behind
mitigations.notes: Three web shells were found, two outside the initial scope.

mitigations.action: Block the exfiltration destination and throttle large outbound transfers
mitigations.notes: Applied too late; most data had already left.

mitigations.action: Place the public-facing application behind a WAF with virtual patching
Alert on abnormal outbound data volume per user or per host
mitigations.notes: Would have cut 11 days of dwell time to hours.

mitigations.action: Introduce mandatory pre-release SAST and dependency scanning

incidents.title: Password spraying against remote access — government agency
incidents.text: A government agency reported password spraying against its remote access portal on 5 December 2024. The attacker attempted a small number of common passwords against 4,200 accounts from a rotating set of source addresses including 92.63.197.153. Four accounts were compromised. MFA fatigue prompts were then pushed to one of the accounts until a user approved. The attacker performed account discovery and directory enumeration before being detected. No data was exfiltrated. Handled by Officer Abdullah Alnasser.

mitigations.action: Lock targeted accounts and block the source ranges
mitigations.notes: Source rotation limited the value of IP blocking.

mitigations.action: Disable the compromised account and revoke all active sessions and tokens
Switch from push-based MFA to number matching or FIDO2 keys
mitigations.notes: Deployed within three weeks; no repeat approvals since.

mitigations.action: Enforce account lockout thresholds and deploy MFA on all external logins
Alert on repeated denied MFA prompts for a single account
Alert on high-volume authentication failures across many accounts from one source

incidents.title: Insider data theft before resignation — technology
incidents.text: A software company identified insider data theft on 11 June 2025. A departing employee in engineering collected source code and customer databases over three weeks and uploaded them to personal cloud storage. The activity used valid credentials and no malware. Data theft was confirmed for roughly 40 GB. The employee's manager, Eng. Rakan Alsudairi, escalated after noticing unusual repository access from the account rakan.dev@company-example.io on host LAP-ENG-221.

mitigations.action: Preserve endpoint and cloud audit logs before revoking access
mitigations.notes: Evidence preservation before lockout was decisive for the legal case.

mitigations.action: Disable the compromised account and revoke all active sessions and tokens
Block unsanctioned cloud storage domains at the proxy
Deploy DLP policies covering uploads to personal cloud storage
Trigger enhanced monitoring automatically when a resignation is filed
Alert on large upload to a personal cloud-storage service

incidents.title: DDoS against public services — telecom
incidents.text: Etisal Telecom Group experienced a distributed denial of service attack on 2 July 2025. A traffic flood peaking at 780 Gbps targeted the subscriber self-service portal, causing service disruption for approximately five hours. No intrusion, malware or data exfiltration was identified. The attack was mitigated with upstream scrubbing. Reported by Manager Ibrahim Aldosari at noc@etisal-telecom.sa.

mitigations.action: Enable upstream scrubbing with the ISP and rate-limit at the edge
Fail over the portal to a CDN-fronted static status page
Pre-arrange DDoS mitigation capacity and rehearse failover
mitigations.notes: Activation took 90 minutes because the runbook had never been exercised.

incidents.title: Infostealer malware and credential resale — retail
incidents.text: A retail chain identified infostealer malware on a point of sale management workstation on 19 August 2025. The user executed a trojan disguised as an invoice attachment. The malware performed credential dumping from the browser and keylogging, then exfiltrated the data over an encrypted channel to 5.188.206.77. Stolen credentials later appeared for sale. Corporate VPN credentials were among those compromised. Contact Analyst Wafa Alsubaie, wafa.alsubaie@retail-example.com, host POS-MGT-14.

mitigations.action: Isolate affected endpoints from the network immediately
Force a password reset for every credential stored in the affected browser profile
Rebuild the affected host from a known-good image
Block macro execution in documents originating from the internet
Prohibit browser credential storage via policy and deploy a managed password manager
Monitor credential marketplaces for corporate domains

incidents.title: Ransomware via exposed RDP — logistics
incidents.text: Najd Ports Logistics reported ransomware on 30 September 2025. The attacker gained access through exposed RDP on a jump server with a weak password, using brute force over two days from 45.135.232.19. They escalated privileges with a local privilege escalation exploit, cleared event logs, deleted backups, and files were encrypted across the container tracking systems. Operations halted for 22 hours. Managed by CISO Mohammed Alqarni, m.alqarni@najdports.sa, affected host SRV-JUMP-02.

mitigations.action: Isolate affected endpoints from the network immediately
Remove direct RDP exposure; require VPN plus MFA
mitigations.notes: Root cause. Should never have been internet-facing.

mitigations.action: Force a domain-wide credential reset, including krbtgt twice
Restore from the most recent verified-clean offline backup
mitigations.notes: Two weeks of tracking data was lost; backup frequency was inadequate.

mitigations.action: Forward logs off-host in real time so local deletion cannot destroy evidence
Maintain immutable, air-gapped backups and rehearse restore times

incidents.title: Cloud data exposure through leaked API key — technology
incidents.text: A SaaS provider disclosed a data breach on 8 October 2025 after an API key was committed to a public code repository. The key, AKIAJ4TESTKEYEXAMPLE, allowed read access to an object store containing customer exports. An external party enumerated and downloaded roughly 12,000 records over an encrypted channel. There was no malware and no endpoint compromise. Regulatory notification obligations were triggered. Reported by CTO Lina Alghamdi at lina@saas-example.io.

mitigations.action: Revoke the exposed key and rotate every credential in the same scope
Review object store access logs to establish the full scope of access
Enable secret scanning with push protection on all repositories
mitigations.notes: Blocked four further secret commits in the following month.

mitigations.action: Move to short-lived, workload-scoped credentials instead of static keys
Alert on object store access from outside known network ranges

incidents.title: Phishing attachment leading to remote access trojan — energy
incidents.text: An energy sector operator detected a remote access trojan on 12 November 2025. Initial access came from a phishing email with a malicious attachment; the macro-enabled document was opened by a user in the engineering team and spawned an obfuscated PowerShell command. A backdoor established C2 beaconing to 194.36.191.68. The attacker performed system information discovery and remote system discovery before containment. No lateral movement into the SCADA environment was achieved and no data was exfiltrated. Reported by Eng. Sultan Albaqami on host WKSTN-ENG-051.

mitigations.action: Isolate affected endpoints from the network immediately
mitigations.notes: Detected within 25 minutes; this is why it went no further.

mitigations.action: Pull the malicious attachment from every mailbox that received it
Sinkhole the C2 domain and block the destination at the egress firewall
Block macro execution in documents originating from the internet
Enable PowerShell script-block and module logging, forward to the SIEM
mitigations.notes: The detection that caught this incident.

mitigations.action: Segment the OT network from corporate IT with an enforced boundary

incidents.title: Ransomware halted before encryption — finance
incidents.text: Sahm Capital Investment Bank contained a ransomware intrusion on 21 January 2026 before encryption occurred. Initial access was through a spearphishing link that harvested credentials from an employee in the finance department. The attacker signed in with valid accounts, ran encoded PowerShell, and attempted to disable the EDR agent, which triggered a tamper-protection alert. Attempted lateral movement over SMB shares was blocked by network segmentation. Shadow copy deletion was attempted and blocked by application control. No files were encrypted and no data was exfiltrated. Reported by Analyst Reem Alkhalifa, r.alkhalifa@sahmcapital.sa, from 178.62.44.19.

mitigations.action: Isolate affected endpoints from the network immediately
mitigations.notes: Full containment in 12 minutes from the tamper-protection alert.

mitigations.action: Disable the compromised account and revoke all active sessions and tokens
Enable tamper protection on all endpoint security agents
mitigations.notes: The control that turned a breach into a near-miss.

mitigations.action: Restrict vssadmin/wbadmin execution to administrators via application control
Alert whenever an EDR agent stops reporting or a security service is stopped
Enforce phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn) for all users
